title: Quantum uncertainty in a macroscopic domain
abstract: We develop a classical model-theoretic representation of partial Boolean algebras and use it to formulate quantum-like uncertainty without abandoning classical propositional logic. Given a surjection from the initial formulæ of a propositional language onto a partial Boolean algebra $(\mathcal V,Π)$, we construct a consistent theory $\mathcal T_g$ whose core---the ordered set of equivalence classes of initial formulæ---is isomorphic to $(\mathcal V,Π)$. Its models are characterized as upward-closed clusters, yielding a model-theoretic formulation of KS-colourability: an $n$-dimensional partial Boolean algebra is KS-colourable exactly when the induced theory has a model meeting every pre-frame in one primitive formula.   For finite-spectrum observables, uncertainty is defined by the number of locally admissible atomic outcomes. Dispersion-free models are characterized by the singleton pre-frame condition. With an additional measurement-update postulate, a finite example shows how measurement of an incompatible observable can destroy sharpness, providing a model-theoretic form of back-action. A $12$-vertex partial Boolean algebra is KS-colourable, whereas a rigorously constructed $140$-vertex, four-dimensional partial Boolean algebra is not, as shown by a parity argument; its incidence structure is isomorphic to the Peres $24$-ray, $24$-basis configuration in $\mathbb R^4$. Macroscopic interpretations show that these phenomena arise from the organization of propositions and models rather than from nonclassical deduction. Finally, we relate certain models to the probability-one propositions of pure states and density operators, while emphasizing that such certainty models do not determine the full quantum state.
summary: This work develops a model-theoretic framework using partial Boolean algebras to mathematically encode concepts of quantum uncertainty. By analyzing the structure of these algebras, the authors show how classical logical consistency can yield analogues of measurement back-action and contextuality. It provides an abstract structural understanding of quantum constraints rooted in propositional logic.
main_problem: The paper aims to formulate quantum-like uncertainty using purely classical model-theoretic tools, specifically by representing partial Boolean algebras.
main_result: It establishes that certain structural properties (KS-colourability) of these abstract algebras correspond to physical constraints like the destruction of sharpness upon measurement back-action.
method: The authors develop a framework mapping propositional logic theories onto partial Boolean algebras, using model theory to define concepts analogous to quantum compatibility and uncertainty.
model_or_system: The system is an abstract mathematical model based on partial Boolean algebras derived from the core of consistent theories in classical propositional logic. These structures are then mapped analogously to propositions associated with physical observables.
key_observables: KS-colourability, sharpness (number of locally admissible atomic outcomes), and the structure of the underlying partial Boolean algebra.
important_parameters: The dimension of the partial Boolean algebra (e.g., 12-vertex vs. 140-vertex) dictates whether certain structural properties hold.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that quantum uncertainty can be captured by analyzing the organization and compatibility structure of propositions within a classical logical setting, rather than requiring nonclassical deduction itself.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Hasse diagram of small partial Boolean algebras (like $V_{12}$) formed by gluing together smaller Boolean components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the model-theoretic representation of partial Boolean algebras, to characterizing uncertainty via KS-colourability and measurement back-action in finite examples, concluding with connections to state support sets and limitations regarding probability assignment.
why_interesting: It offers a highly abstract, logic-based approach to contextuality and quantum constraints, which could provide novel mathematical tools for understanding non-classical correlations without invoking Hilbert space formalism directly.
